As we wrap up, I want you to think back on the stories we've walked through together—the heartbreak, the betrayals, and the courage it takes to survive.
History isn’t just a list of dates. It’s living memory—carried by people who refuse to let it fade away. The journey in Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee isn’t just a look at the past. It’s a real call to see, to listen, and to act with empathy right now.
So, what should you carry with you from all of this?
Broken promises leave scars that can last for generations and shape who we are. Survival isn’t just about getting by—it’s about holding on to dignity, even in the darkest times. Our stories and cultures are lifelines, especially when the world tries to erase them. True justice begins with listening—really listening—to stories that have been pushed aside. And hope, though it can feel fragile, is often the spark that moves people forward.
Moving forward, let these lessons remind you that every community carries its own history of struggle and resilience. The next time someone shares their pain, or you witness injustice, pause. Listen. Ask yourself what you can do to honor their experience.
Even small acts of remembrance, kindness, and advocacy truly do matter.
The legacy of Wounded Knee isn’t just a warning from long ago; it’s a guide for creating a kinder, more just world. Even when change feels impossible, remember—healing starts with memory, and hope survives as long as we keep telling the story and refuse to let it end.
